name: pagination
title: Pagination
description: Page links as drawn buttons: each number is a Button around your own link, the page you are on is a block of highlighter, the arrows and the ellipsis are hand-drawn. It is just links, so it works with any router, or with plain hrefs and no JavaScript at all.

a11y: A `nav` landmark labelled "pagination" holding a list of links. The current page has `aria-current="page"`; it is also bold-on-highlighter, so it does not rely on colour.

Previous and Next carry `aria-label`s that name their destination, so they read the same when the word is hidden on a phone. Give number links an accessible name of their own when the bare number is ambiguous (`aria-label="Page 3"`).
A disabled link is `aria-disabled`, removed from the tab order and drawn as the dashed alternative; its click is prevented and your `onClick` is not called.
Each link is at least 36 px square (32 compact, 28 calm), a tab stop with the theme's drawn blue focus ring. Being plain anchors, they work without JavaScript and with any router.
meta.usage:
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationEllipsis,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from "@/components/ui/pagination"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Pagination>
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=1">1</PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=2" isActive>
            2
          </PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationEllipsis />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext href="?page=3" />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  )
}
